topics.display_title: Enlightenment and Age of Revolutions Overview

panels.title: Enlightenment starting condition
ascii_lines: INHERITED AUTHORITY -> Church, dynasty, privilege by birth
NEW TEST -> reason, nature, humanity, freedom, happiness
POLITICAL QUESTION -> by what right does power command?
RESULT -> authority must justify itself in public terms

panels.title: Thinker-to-institution map
ascii_lines: LOCKE -> natural rights + consent -> limited government
MONTESQUIEU -> separation of powers -> constitutional restraint
ROUSSEAU -> popular sovereignty -> people as source of authority
VOLTAIRE -> clerical criticism -> secular public debate
source_references: Locke: rights, consent and limited rule

panels.title: Ideas, crisis and force
ascii_lines: IDEAS -> make inherited privilege illegitimate
CRISIS -> fiscal stress, food stress, imperial grievance
MOBILISATION -> assemblies, pamphlets, crowds, organised groups
REVOLUTION -> legitimacy + momentum + force must interact

panels.title: Parallel Atlantic routes
ascii_lines: AMERICA -> external empire challenged -> federal republic
FRANCE -> internal privilege challenged -> social-legal rupture
SHARED -> rights, consent, sovereignty, constitutional argument
DIFFERENCE -> America broke a link; France broke a structure
source_references: America and France on the same axes

panels.title: Rights and exclusions ledger
ascii_lines: UNIVERSAL CLAIM -> rights belong to human beings or citizens
EARLY BOUNDARY -> property, race, sex and colonial status restrict membership
CONTRADICTION -> proclaimed equality outruns political practice
LEGACY -> excluded groups later use the same grammar to demand entry

panels.title: Liberalism versus conservatism
ascii_lines: LIBERALISM -> consent, rights, law, representation
CONSERVATISM -> order, property, religion, gradual change
LIBERAL RISK -> restricted franchise and imperial compatibility
CONSERVATIVE RISK -> censorship and dynastic repression

panels.title: Nationalism's changing alliances
ascii_lines: CORE -> nation claimed as proper unit of sovereignty
LIBERAL ALLIANCE -> constitutions and national self-rule
CONSERVATIVE USE -> state-led unification and discipline
LATER FORMS -> racial, imperial and anti-colonial nationalisms

panels.title: Capitalism's social mechanism
ascii_lines: PRIVATE OWNERSHIP + PROFIT -> investment and factory production
WAGE LABOUR -> workers depend on employers for livelihood
OUTPUT GROWTH -> productive capacity and consumption expand
UNREGULATED COST -> insecurity, long hours and class conflict

panels.title: Socialist family tree
ascii_lines: SOCIALISM -> social ownership or control; many methods
COMMUNISM -> revolution + central planning + one-party practice
SOCIAL DEMOCRACY -> elections + regulation + redistribution
TEST -> ask who owns, who decides and by what method

panels.title: Labour pressure becomes law
ascii_lines: 1824 -> England repeals anti-union laws
1830s-40s -> Chartism links labour to franchise
TRADE UNIONS -> collective bargaining enters modern politics
FACTORY LAW -> laissez-faire yields to evidence of harm
source_references: Trade unions and the constitutional social question

panels.title: Welfare-state causal synthesis
ascii_lines: PROGRAMME -> socialist and labour demands for security
OPENING -> depression destroys private safeguards
CAPACITY -> total war expands administration and solidarity
OUTPUT -> Social Security 1935; Beveridge Report 1942
source_references: The welfare-state synthesis and final verdict

panels.title: Overview answer spine
ascii_lines: DEFINE -> Enlightenment climate or named doctrine
EVIDENCE -> thinker, document, institution and social base
ANALYSE -> form, timing, depth and effect on society
QUALIFY -> exclusions, variant forms and non-linear outcomes
source_references: The welfare-state synthesis and final verdict

panels.title: Imperial grievance system
ascii_lines: 1763 WAR DEBT -> tighter British taxation and regulation
MERCANTILISM -> shipping, market and manufacturing constraints
WESTWARD LIMITS -> land grievance plus Native dispossession
ASSEMBLIES -> existing institutions convert grievance into resistance

panels.title: Constitutional taxation dispute
ascii_lines: BRITISH CLAIM -> Parliament may tax the colonies
COLONIAL CLAIM -> assemblies represent colonial taxpayers
STAMP ACT 1765 -> principle becomes explicit
OUTCOME -> fiscal protest becomes a sovereignty dispute

panels.title: Protest becomes common action
ascii_lines: 1773 -> Boston Tea Party
1774 -> First Continental Congress, Philadelphia
1775 -> Lexington and Concord
1776 -> Declaration turns resistance into independence

panels.title: Three actors, three functions
ascii_lines: JEFFERSON -> drafts the Declaration
PAINE -> Common Sense supplies popular ideological force
WASHINGTON -> commands American armies
RULE -> do not exchange authorship, argument and command

panels.title: War internationalises
ascii_lines: SARATOGA 1777 -> colonial survival becomes credible
FRENCH ALLIANCE 1778 -> money, arms, fleet and wider war
BRITAIN -> faces pressure beyond North America
YORKTOWN 1781 -> decisive military turning point

panels.title: Victory, recognition, constitution
ascii_lines: YORKTOWN 1781 -> military decision
TREATY OF PARIS 1783 -> legal recognition
CONSTITUTION 1789 -> durable federal state form
BILL OF RIGHTS -> liberties entrenched against government

panels.title: Declaration versus Constitution
ascii_lines: DECLARATION 1776 -> why independence is legitimate
ARTICLES PHASE 1781 -> states cooperate under weak union
CONSTITUTION 1789 -> how federal power is organised
BILL OF RIGHTS -> what government is forbidden to violate

panels.title: Political revolution ledger
ascii_lines: EMPIRE -> rejected
MONARCHY -> replaced by federal republic
WRITTEN CONSTITUTION -> state powers placed in a text
RIGHTS -> become standards of legitimate government

panels.title: Social limits ledger
ascii_lines: SLAVERY -> survives
FRANCHISE -> property and status restrictions remain
WOMEN -> no equivalent political citizenship
NATIVE PEOPLES -> expansion intensifies dispossession

panels.title: World-historical export
ascii_lines: ANTI-IMPERIAL CLAIM -> rebellion justified through rights
REPUBLIC -> survives war and diplomatic recognition
WRITTEN CONSTITUTION -> becomes an exportable state model
INFLUENCE -> France, Europe and Latin America observe the precedent

panels.title: America versus France
ascii_lines: AMERICA -> breaks external imperial authority
FRANCE -> attacks internal privilege and feudal order
AMERICA -> constitutional stability
FRANCE -> deeper social rupture and radicalisation

panels.title: Qualified American verdict
ascii_lines: CAUSE -> empire, taxation, assemblies, rights
COURSE -> protest, war, alliance, treaty
CREATION -> written federal republic
QUALIFICATION -> slavery and exclusion survive
